info.description:
This is the Nortezh platform's public, user-facing API — the same
surface a service account (see serviceaccount.createKey below) or an
external script calls directly. It is NOT REST: every route is a POST
to a dot-notation path (e.g. POST /user/disk.create) with a JSON
request body, built on github.com/acoshift/arpc/v2. Read this before
trusting any status code shown below:

- Success is always HTTP 200: {"ok":true,"result":<...>}.
- A domain error (the @Failure codes listed per route, e.g.
DISK_NOT_FOUND) is ALSO HTTP 200, body {"ok":false,"error":
{"code":"...","message":"..."}}. Do not assume 4xx for a documented
error code — arpc reports domain errors as 200 with ok:false by
design, so your client must check "ok", not the status.
- A request whose params fail validation gets the same HTTP-200-with-
ok:false treatment, code VALIDATE_ERROR, with an extra "items" array
of one message per failed field.
- Malformed JSON or an unsupported Content-Type is HTTP 400.
- Anything unexpected is HTTP 500 with a generic, empty error body —
the real error is logged server-side but never exposed to the caller.

Authenticate with EITHER scheme below on every route except
payment.channel (deliberately public, no credentials accepted) and this
docs UI itself.

post.description:
Returns the profile of whichever account authenticated the request.
Every authenticated screen in the frontend calls this first; the
phoneVerified field is what gates the rest of the product. Takes no
request parameters — identity comes entirely from the Authorization
credentials.

There is no dedicated "account not found" error code: if the
authenticated account id no longer has a matching row (should not
happen in practice), this falls through to the generic HTTP 500
described in the API-level description above.

default.description: UNAUTHORIZED — missing, malformed, or expired/invalid credentials

post.description:
Returns billings.credit_balance directly, as a bare decimal string (see
.swaggo — decimal.Decimal marshals as a quoted string). This is the
settled balance (as of the last settlement run), NOT the live balance
(today's accrued usage is not subtracted) — see billing.get/billing.me
for both figures side by side if the live number matters.

Known gap: request field is "ID" (capital, no json tag), not "id" like
every other route's id parameter. A separate known gap: if ID fails
validation (nil UUID), the handler currently discards that error and
returns a successful result of "0" rather than VALIDATE_ERROR — so
VALIDATE_ERROR is listed here only in principle; in the current code it
is never actually returned.

though the row is inserted with status active — the create response
does not reflect the account's real, just-created status. Call
billing.me or billing.get afterward for the accurate value.

post.description:
Rate-limited to one call per minute per billing account
(BILLING_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if the last topup transaction for this
account started under a minute ago). Writes a pending
billing_transactions row (category topup) and asks the payment gateway
for a pay URL; the account's balance is only credited later, when the
Ksher webhook confirms payment against the returned reference.

Known gap: request fields are capitalized — "ID", "Amount", "Channel",
"RedirectURL" — not the lowerCamelCase used by every other route (no
json tags on this params struct). A separate known gap: Channel is
checked with a substring test against "promptpay card truemoney
linepay" rather than an exact match, so some non-channel values pass
validation and fail later at the gateway instead.

Errors (every one of these is HTTP 200 with ok:false):
- BILLING_NOT_FOUND — ID does not match a billing account the caller owns
- BILLING_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED — a topup was already started for this account less than 1 minute ago
- VALIDATE_ERROR — ID/Amount/Channel missing, amount not positive, RedirectURL not a valid URL, or Channel not (a substring match of) a known channel

post.description:
Binds a GitHub repository, at a branch or tag plus a Dockerfile path, to a
deployment — the first step of building that deployment's image from
source. There is no update route: to change anything about a binding,
delete it (cicd.delete) and create a new one. A deployment may carry only
one binding at a time.

This route only records the binding — there is currently no route to
trigger a build or deploy from it; building the image from the bound
repository is not yet available through this API.

create verifies the repository actually exists and is visible through the
named installation by calling GitHub live — a syntactically valid-looking
repoFullName can still fail with CICD_REPO_NOT_FOUND if the App simply
isn't installed on that repo (wrong org, or repo access not granted to the
installation).

Errors (every one of these is HTTP 200 with ok:false):
- PROJECT_NOT_FOUND — project does not exist or the caller is not a member
- GITHUB_NOT_FOUND — installationId is not linked to the calling account
- CICD_INSTALLATION_SUSPENDED — the installation is suspended on GitHub
(can't mint a token to verify the repo)
- CICD_DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND — deploymentId does not belong to this project
- CICD_DEPLOYMENT_ALREADY_BOUND — the deployment already has a binding;
delete it first
- CICD_REPO_NOT_FOUND — repoFullName is not visible to this installation
- GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REVOKED — GitHub reports the installation as
revoked/uninstalled while verifying the repository
- GITHUB_UPSTREAM — GitHub was unreachable or errored while verifying the
repository (transient — retry)
- VALIDATE_ERROR — params failed validation; error.items lists each
failed rule

parameters.description: Repository/branch/Dockerfile to bind to a deployment
parameters.name: body

post.description:
Provisions a managed Mongo instance. Managed databases are immutable
after creation — there is no update route; to change anything, delete and
recreate. get and delete key on {project,name}, not the id this call
returns.

Provisioning is asynchronous: this call only stamps the request and
returns an id right away. Poll db.mongo.get with {project,name} and watch
its host/port fields — both stay empty until the per-cluster deployer
applies the kdb custom resource and the kdb operator finishes
provisioning, at which point host/port are filled in and actionStatus
becomes 2 (success — actionStatus is a plain integer on the wire, 1 =
pending, 2 = success, not the string its name suggests).

Requires the target cluster's `database` feature to be enabled — call
cluster.list beforehand and check features.database (present = enabled)
for the location you intend to use.

Errors (every one of these is HTTP 200 with ok:false):
- PROJECT_NOT_FOUND — project does not exist or the caller is not a member
- DATABASE_CLUSTER_NOT_SUPPORTED — the target cluster does not have the
database feature enabled
- DATABASE_PROJECT_ACCESS_DENIED — the project's billing account is not
allowed to use this cluster
- DATABASE_NAME_NOT_AVAILABLE — a database with this name already
exists in the project
- VALIDATE_ERROR — params failed validation; error.items lists each
failed rule

default.description: Domain error — always HTTP 200 with ok:false. Codes: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, DATABASE_CLUSTER_NOT_SUPPORTED, DATABASE_PROJECT_ACCESS_DENIED, DATABASE_NAME_NOT_AVAILABLE, VALIDATE_ERROR.

project

failed rule

record), and `errors` lists anything currently wrong with it.

first step of the mandatory phone verification onboarding flow — the
frontend blocks the rest of the product until auth.me reports
phoneVerified: true.

Real constraints enforced by the handler (not by Params.Valid — this
route has none; validation is manual):
- Phone must normalize to E.164 or the call fails with PHONE_INVALID.
- Only one active OTP per account: requesting again within 15 seconds
of the previous request fails with PHONE_OTP_ACTIVE (unless the
previous OTP was already verified, or its wait window has passed).
- The phone number must not already be verified on another account, or
the call fails with PHONE_ALREADY_USED.
- The OTP expires 5 minutes after this call succeeds.

post.description:

as verified (auth.me's phoneVerified becomes true).

Real constraints enforced by the handler (Params has no Valid() method;
everything below is manual, in-handler validation):
- Phone must normalize to E.164 or the call fails with PHONE_INVALID.
- The pending OTP row is looked up by account id, not by phone — if
there is none, or its phone does not match, this fails with
PHONE_OTP_INVALID (the same code as a wrong OTP code, so a client
cannot distinguish "no OTP pending" from "wrong code").
- The OTP expires 5 minutes after it was requested (PHONE_OTP_EXPIRED).
- Maximum 3 verify attempts per requested OTP (PHONE_MAX_ATTEMPTS); a
failed attempt for any reason (wrong code, expired, provider error)
increments the attempt counter.
- If the OTP was already verified, this call is idempotent and returns
the original result without re-checking anything.

api_auth.ProfileResult.description: Account profile of the currently authenticated caller.

phone.description:
Phone is the verified phone number in E.164 format (e.g. "+66812345678"), or null
if the account has never completed phone verification.

phoneVerified.description:
PhoneVerified gates the rest of the product: the frontend blocks every other
screen behind onboarding (phone.requestOTP / phone.verifyOTP) until this is true.

phoneVerifiedAt.description: PhoneVerifiedAt is null until PhoneVerified is true.

liveCreditBalance.description:
LiveCreditBalance is credit_balance minus today's accrued project_billings for
every project under this account — i.e. the balance as of right now, including
usage that has happened today but has not yet been deducted by the billing
worker (which runs every 30 minutes and only settles the previous day). This is
the number to show as "current balance" in a UI.

settledCreditBalance.description:
SettledCreditBalance is the raw stored credit_balance column: the balance as of
the last time the settlement job actually deducted usage from it (settlement is
one-shot per UTC day, for the previous day). It does not reflect today's
still-accruing usage. LiveCreditBalance is almost always the more useful number;
SettledCreditBalance is exposed for reconciliation against settlement records.

status.description: Status marshals as a string, not a number.

trial.description:
Trial mirrors the account's is_trial column; trial accounts are subject to
separate cluster/feature restrictions elsewhere in the API (see cluster.list).

api_billing.GetTransactionResult.description: Known gap: Type is only ever set to "topup", "transfer_in" or "transfer_out" (categories 0/1/2) — the "deduct" and "add" categories (3/4, see the enum list on billing.listTransaction) are not mapped here, so a transaction of either kind comes back with type: "" (empty string). "usage" is never produced despite what an older comment on this field used to claim.

id.description:
ID is the transaction's numeric row id, marshaled as a JSON string (`,string`
tag), e.g. "1024" not 1024.

type.description:
Type is "topup", "transfer_in" or "transfer_out" — see the known gap on the
containing type doc for the categories this does NOT cover.

api_billing.InvoiceResult.description: Every money field here is a pre-formatted decimal string (two decimal places, e.g. "107.00"), not a numeric type — these are display-ready strings, not decimal.Decimal values.  Known gap: FinancialInfo.NetAmount is the transaction's raw amount and FinancialInfo.GrossAmount is amount minus the computed VAT — i.e. Gross is smaller than Net here, the reverse of the usual "gross = net + VAT" convention. Read the two fields by their actual formula, not their name.

billingAddress.description:
BillingAddress is populated from the billing account's tax fields (taxNo,
taxName, address) as they stood at the time the transaction's metadata was
written — not the account's current tax fields. If those were never set on the
transaction, this falls back to a 13-digit zero taxId, "N/A" company name, and
"N/A" address.

grossAmount.description:
GrossAmount is NetAmount minus VatAmount — see the known gap on the
containing type doc.

netAmount.description: NetAmount is the transaction's raw amount, before the VAT computation below.

vatAmount.description: VatAmount is NetAmount * 0.07, rounded to 2 decimal places.

vatRate.description: VatRate is always the literal string "7%".

documentNo.description:
DocumentNo is INV<YYYYMMDD><6-digit-zero-padded-transaction-id>, e.g.
"INV20260726000042" — the date is the transaction's created_at (UTC), and the
6-digit suffix is the transaction's own row id, not a per-day counter.

orderItems.description:
OrderItems has exactly one line item: the transaction itself, named by its
transaction category (e.g. "topup").

api_billing.Item.description: One of the caller's billing accounts, as returned by billing.me.

liveCreditBalance.description:
LiveCreditBalance is credit_balance minus today's accrued project_billings —
see Billing.LiveCreditBalance for the full explanation.

settledCreditBalance.description:

envGroups.description:
EnvGroups is an ordered list of env-group names (see envgroup.create) to merge into this
deployment's environment: groups merge in the order given (a later group overrides an earlier
one on key conflict), then this deployment's own Env/AddEnv/RemoveEnv result is overlaid on top
and always wins. The merge is baked into the new revision's spec at deploy time — editing a
group afterwards does not affect an already-running deployment until it is redeployed. nil
(the field absent) leaves the deployment's current group links unchanged; [] clears them. An
unknown group name fails with DEPLOYMENT_ENV_GROUP_NOT_FOUND.

googleAuth.description:
GoogleAuth gates this deployment's public (external) URL behind Google login, restricted to an
allowlist. Only valid when enabled=true, Type is WebService (or omitted) and Internal is not
true; the allowlist (allowedEmails + allowedDomains combined) must be non-empty and at most 200
entries. The target cluster must also advertise the web-google-auth feature (see cluster.list)
for the gate to actually be enforced.

image.description:
Image is a fully-qualified, pinned container image reference (must not end in "@" — a bare
digest prefix with nothing after it is rejected).

internal.description: internal service: true hides the deployment from the public ingress (also required for InternalTCPService)

protocol.description:
Protocol only applies to WebService (Worker/CronJob must leave it none). Marshals as its name,
never as a number — sending an empty string or an unlisted name fails with
DEPLOYMENT_INVALID_PROTOCOL. Omit the field to get the type's default (http for WebService,
none otherwise).

resource.description:
Resources sets cpu/memory requests and cpu/memory limits. Requests must match one of the
target cluster's advertised allocatable values (see cluster.list) or the route fails with
DEPLOYMENT_INVALID_CPU / DEPLOYMENT_INVALID_MEMORY / DEPLOYMENT_INVALID_CPU_LIMIT.

schedule.description: cronjob schedule (crontab syntax, required and validated only when type is CronJob)

sidecars.description:
Sidecars are optional extra containers alongside the main one, at most 2. Only the Cloud SQL
Proxy kind currently exists: sidecars: [{"cloudSqlProxy":{"instance":"...","port":3300,
"credentials":"..."}}] — instance is required, port defaults to 3300, credentials is optional
(a service-account JSON key). ⚠ Connect to it with sslmode=disable: the proxy terminates TLS to
Cloud SQL itself and exposes a plaintext local socket, but Go's lib/pq defaults to
sslmode=require and will fail with "pq: SSL is not enabled on the server" otherwise.

name, never as a number — sending an empty string or an unlisted name fails with
DEPLOYMENT_INVALID_TYPE. The legacy numeric value 4 ("TCPService") is deprecated and can no
longer be created or referenced by name; it is not in the accepted set below.
